bands.label: Exemplar
bands.blurb: Reference-quality API operations across every facet.

companies.name: Salla
companies.description: Salla is a Saudi Arabia-based e-commerce platform — often called the Shopify of the Middle East — that lets merchants launch, operate, and grow Arabic-first online stores without code. Founded in 2016 in Makkah by Nawaf Hariri and Salman Butt, Salla now powers more than 80,000 active stores. The platform exposes a Merchant REST API (https://api.salla.dev/admin/v2), an OAuth 2.0 Partners authorization service, signed webhooks for the full storefront lifecycle, a Shipping and Fulfillment app contract, the Twilight theme engine and JavaScript SDK, the Salla CLI, and official starter kits for PHP/Laravel and Node.js/Express. Backed by Sanabil (PIF), STV, Investcorp, Vision Ventures, and Raed Ventures, Salla raised a $130M pre-IPO round in 2024.

bands.label: Strong
bands.blurb: Solid contracts, transparent operations, and an easy start.

companies.name: Lean Technologies
companies.description: Lean Technologies is a MENA open finance and payments infrastructure platform serving the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. Its APIs let businesses connect to customers' bank accounts to read financial data (accounts, balances, transactions, identity, income and credit insights) and to move money via pay-by-bank payments, Account-on-File consents, payment links, payouts, refunds and scheduled payments. Lean provides the LinkSDK client for web, iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter, a FAPI-grade OAuth 2.0 authorization server, webhooks, a hosted documentation MCP server, and public Postman collections. Lean is regulated under the UAE Open Finance (CBUAE) and Saudi Open Banking (SAMA) frameworks and is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified.

companies.name: Paymob
companies.description: Paymob is a Cairo-headquartered, licensed payment infrastructure provider for the MENAP region. Serving roughly 390,000 merchants across Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Pakistan (with Qatar announced), Paymob unifies card acquiring, regional mobile wallets (Vodafone Cash, Etisalat Cash, Orange Money, STC Pay, Oman Net, EasyPaisa, JazzCash), BNPL rails (Tabby, Tamara, valU, Souhoola, Forsa, Aman), Apple Pay, Google Pay, POS terminals, subscriptions, installments, marketplace payouts, mass disbursement (Paymob Send), and an end-to-end cashless commerce platform (Paymob Sync) behind a single Accept / Intentions API surface.

companies.name: Unifonic
companies.description: Unifonic is a Saudi Arabia-based customer engagement and CPaaS platform, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, that powers SMS, WhatsApp, voice, push notification, and OTP-verification communication for enterprises across the Middle East and beyond. Its developer surface spans an SMS (NextGen) REST API, an Authenticate API for multi-channel OTP verification, Voice APIs for calls, IVR, and number masking, and a WhatsApp Conversations API with template, session, and management endpoints, alongside webhooks for delivery status and channel events, mobile push SDKs, a web event-tracking SDK, chatbot and Flow Studio automation products, and a WhatsApp sandbox for testing.

companies.name: Tamara
companies.description: Tamara is the Saudi Arabia–headquartered MENA shopping and Buy-Now-Pay-Later platform offering Shariah-compliant split-payment and Pay-Now solutions across Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman. Founded in 2020 and licensed by SAMA (Saudi Central Bank), Tamara provides merchants with a hosted-checkout Direct API, in-store SMS and QR payment links, mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, Flutter, and React Native, plug-and-play e-commerce extensions for Shopify, Magento, OpenCart, PrestaShop, Salesforce Commerce Cloud and WooCommerce, webhooks for order and dispute lifecycle events, and a Channel Partners onboarding API for payment service providers and platforms that white-label Tamara. The company became the first homegrown Saudi fintech unicorn in December 2023 after raising a US$340M Series C led by SNB Capital and Sanabil Investments and is backed by debt facilities from Goldman Sachs, Citi, and Apollo for its Shariah-compliant funding base.

bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

companies.name: Lean Technologies
companies.description: Lean Technologies is a Middle East Open Banking and Open Finance infrastructure provider founded in 2019 and headquartered in the UAE. Lean offers regulated Account Information (AIS), Payment Initiation (PIS), payouts, refunds, account and name verifications, and derived insights across the UAE and Saudi Arabia, with verification coverage extending to 27+ countries globally. Lean holds an In-Principle Approval from the Central Bank of UAE for Open Finance Services (August 2025), a Major Payment Institution licence from the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA), and an FSP licence from the Abu Dhabi Global Market FSRA (no. 200033). The platform is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified and has processed AED 16B+ across 2M+ linked accounts. Investors include Sequoia, General Catalyst, Breyer Capital, Shorooq, Raed, BCV, and Liberty City.

companies.name: Spare
companies.description: Spare is a MENA-region open banking and open finance platform, licensed by the Central Bank of Bahrain as an Account Information Service Provider and Payment Initiation Service Provider (AISP/PISP) and permitted to test under the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) regulatory sandbox. Spare exposes RESTful Account Information Services (AIS) — account details, balances, transactions, statements, beneficiaries, parties, direct debits, plus risk and affordability reports — and Payment Initiation Services (PIS) for domestic single, future-dated and standing-order payments, across separate Bahrain, KSA and UAE tenants hosted in-region for data-residency compliance. Developers authenticate with OAuth2 client credentials to obtain signed JWT bearer tokens, drive a customer to connection to consent to data flow, verify token and webhook signatures against a published JWKS, and integrate via official TypeScript, Java, .NET and PHP SDKs plus Postman collections.

companies.name: EdfaPay, Inc.
companies.description: EdfaPay is a Saudi fintech and payment-technology company offering a developer-friendly payment platform across the GCC region. Its products include a hosted Checkout and Server-to-Server (S2S) payment gateway, SoftPOS tap-to-pay technology that turns mobile devices into card readers, merchant onboarding, payouts, e-invoicing, and white-label solutions for banks and partners. The gateway supports Visa, Mastercard, MADA, Apple Pay and STC Pay with 3D Secure, webhooks, refunds and recurring payments, on PCI-DSS certified infrastructure. EdfaPay was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from its public developer documentation, OpenAPI definitions and SDKs.

companies.name: Tabby
companies.description: Tabby is the MENA region's largest buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) provider, founded in 2019 by Hosam Arab (ex-Namshi) and Daniil Barkalov, originally in Dubai and now headquartered in Riyadh ahead of a planned IPO. Tabby reached a $3.3B valuation in a February 2025 Series E ($160M co-led by Blue Pool Capital and Hassana Investment Company), making it the most valuable fintech in the Middle East, and reports 15M+ users, 40,000+ merchants, and $10B+ in annualized transaction volume across KSA, UAE, and Kuwait. The Tabby API powers split-purchase checkouts (Pay-in-4 interest-free, monthly plans up to 12 months), payment lifecycle management, webhooks, and dispute resolution, complemented by Tabby Card (Visa-enabled), Tabby Shop discovery, Tabby Care purchase protection, and the Tabby Plus loyalty programme. Public developer surface includes a versioned REST API across two regional hosts (api.tabby.ai for UAE/Kuwait, api.tabby.sa for KSA), an OpenAPI 3.1 specification, iOS / Android / Flutter / React Native SDKs, and certified Magento 2, Shopify, WooCommerce, Salla, Zid, OpenCart, ExpandCart, Matjrah, Salesforce, and Odoo plugins.

companies.name: OTO Global
companies.description: OTO is a multi-carrier shipping and fulfillment platform for e-commerce businesses, headquartered in Saudi Arabia and serving 10,000+ merchants. It connects a single integration to 450+ shipping carriers and provides order management, warehouse and picking/packing automation, real-time tracking with customer notifications, returns management, address validation, and omnichannel order synchronization. The OTO REST API V2 (base https://api.tryoto.com/rest/v2, staging at staging-api.tryoto.com) exposes 74 operations across orders, shipments, returns, tracking, shipping rates, carrier integrations, pickup locations, products, stock management, sales channels, and webhooks. Authentication is a bearer access_token minted from a dashboard refresh_token.

companies.name: Reachware Inc.
companies.description: Reachware is an Integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS) that lets separate SaaS and business systems operate as one connected ecosystem, with 200+ prebuilt connectors to systems like NetSuite, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Odoo, SAP, Oracle, Magento, Zid and Qoyod. Alongside the core platform it ships Reach Pay (a payment API for Saudi Arabia payment gateways), Reachware Fatoora (ZATCA e-invoicing), and extension modules for banking, HR, inventory, loyalty and property management. Reach Pay exposes a hosted-redirect REST API for requesting payments, retrieving payment details, refunds and card tokenization. Reachware reports 3,500+ active subscriptions, 300+ customers, 100M+ transactions, and is CMMI Level 3 certified. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Oumla Ltd
companies.description: Oumla is a Saudi-based provider of enterprise-grade digital asset infrastructure for regulated institutions. Its Core API delivers MPC-based wallet and address management, portfolio and native-balance queries, on-chain transaction tracking, smart-contract templates plus deployment and read/write interactions, and tokenization (collections, issue, mint, burn) for tokenized securities, fund units, sukuk, and NFTs. Products span Digital Assets Infrastructure (custody, policy engines, lifecycle), Capital Markets Tokenization, the Oumla Financial Chain for Shariah-compliant interbank settlement, and Bahith blockchain monitoring and compliance analytics built for Saudi data sovereignty. Authentication is via the x-api-key header; long-running mutations run as async workflows. Oumla is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified.

companies.name: Sadq Holding Limited
companies.description: Sadq (صادق) is a Saudi Arabian electronic-signature and digital-trust platform that lets businesses send, sign, and manage legally binding documents online. Its Integration API covers signing envelopes and document packages, signing invitations (email/SMS/link), direct and template-based signing, PKI/e-signing via Saudi Arabia's Nafath national digital identity, document download, reusable templates, users and permissions, signing workflows, webhooks, KYB business verification (commercial-registration checks, Absher OTP, delegacy and national-address lookups), archiving, delegations, and consumption reporting. The platform is fully agent-native — it publishes an OpenAPI schema, an RFC 9727 API catalog, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC discovery metadata, an llms.txt, an auth.md agent-registration guide, and a hosted MCP server. Sadq is a 500 Global portfolio company.

companies.name: King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals
companies.description: King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals (KFUPM) is a public research university in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia, ranked #101 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. KFUPM does not operate a centralized public developer portal, but several institutional systems expose machine-readable interfaces: the KFUPM ePrints theses and dissertations repository serves a live OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint and EPrints REST URLs, and the Elsevier Pure research portal (pure.kfupm.edu.sa) ships the standard Pure Web Services REST API (OpenAPI 3, authentication-gated). KFUPM also maintains a GitHub organization and a student Open Source Club presence.

companies.name: Labayh
companies.description: Labayh (لبيه) is a Saudi Arabian digital mental-health platform delivering online psychological, psychiatric and family counselling to the Arabic-speaking Gulf market. Patients book scheduled or instant video and audio sessions with more than 1,000 licensed specialists, and can also enrol in structured therapeutic programs for depression, anxiety, OCD and social phobia, join peer support groups, take psychological assessments, track mood daily, and watch live and recorded webinars. The company reports over 70 million minutes of consultation delivered. Alongside the consumer app it runs Labayh Business, a corporate employee-wellbeing arm, and Labayh Academy, a training platform for practitioners. Labayh is backed by 500 Global. It operates no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs or developer portal; the API catalogued here is the anonymously readable WordPress REST surface behind labayh.net, whose OpenAPI description API Evangelist derived from the server's own discovery document.

companies.name: Taker
companies.description: Taker is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia-based restaurant technology company (founded 2018, backed by 500 Global) providing an all-in-one online ordering and restaurant-growth platform used by 1,000+ restaurants. Its product suite spans Taker Channels (branded web/mobile ordering), Taker GO (delivery operations), Taker Flow (operations optimization), Taker Grow (marketing automation), and Taker 360 (a unified dashboard across delivery aggregators). The Taker GO delivery-integration API connects restaurants and delivery service providers (DSPs) with bearer-token auth for order creation, tracking, cancellation, and asynchronous status delivery via webhooks, across published sandbox and production environments.

companies.name: Karaz Platform
companies.description: Karaz is an AI-driven Electronic Health Record (EHR) platform based in Saudi Arabia that connects healthcare practitioners, patients, insurance providers, and wellness vendors in a unified health-management ecosystem. It provides real-time biometric and continuous-glucose (CGM) monitoring, AI-driven treatment insights, patient and provider mobile apps, analytics and reporting, rewards and community engagement, and a health-vendor marketplace, with integrations across Apple, Abbott, Medtronic, Dexcom, Roche, Google, and Omron. The Karaz developer API (early-stage) exposes Karaz App and Karaz Care resources over HTTPS with Bearer-token authentication. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public sources.

companies.name: Abwab Ai
companies.description: Abwab.ai is an AI-powered credit intelligence platform for MSME (micro, small, and medium enterprise) lending, used by banks, NBFIs, fintechs, funds, and digital platforms to originate loans, assess credit risk, price, and monitor MSME loan portfolios across the full lending lifecycle. The platform combines rules and AI models for real-time credit decisioning, agentic credit intelligence that surfaces leads and flags portfolio risk, and embedded financing for existing SME platforms. It is API-first, plugging into existing loan-origination and core-banking systems without core replacement, with a versioned REST API (api.abwab.ai), webhook notifications, and Python/Node.js SDKs in development. Abwab is focused on the Saudi Arabian market with in-Kingdom data residency and alignment to the SAMA Cybersecurity Framework, PDPL, and Sharia-compliant lending (used by Kafalah). Backed by Speedinvest.

companies.name: King Abdulaziz University
companies.description: King Abdulaziz University (KAU) is a large public research university in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, ranked #149 in the QS World University Rankings 2025, serving over 100,000 students across 33+ faculties and institutes. Its public web presence runs on the official kau.edu.sa (.gov.sa) domain and includes a beta "Open Data" page, a library/Deanship of Library Affairs portal, and a King Abdulaziz Scientific Platform. KAU operates gated identity infrastructure (an SSO portal at sso.kau.edu.sa and an Oracle Access Manager federation endpoint at iam.kau.edu.sa) but, as of this review, publishes no openly documented, self-service developer API, API reference, or developer portal. There is no official KAU GitHub organization; only a student-run Google Developer Student Club and individual academic projects are present on GitHub.

companies.name: King Saud University
companies.description: King Saud University (KSU) is a public research university in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, founded in 1957, and ranked #200 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. KSU operates a broad estate of digital services — including the Edugate student information system, an LMS, a library catalog, Saudi Digital Library access, a digitized manuscripts portal, and university e-services — but it does not publish a public, documented developer or API program. The systems found during review are end-user web applications gated behind institutional SSO/login rather than openly documented APIs. No public API reference, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or open-data API endpoint could be confirmed.

companies.name: Pemo
companies.description: Pemo is a UAE-based fintech offering smart corporate cards and an all-in-one spend management platform for businesses across the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. The product combines physical and virtual corporate cards with expense management, automated receipt capture, invoice management, and accounting automation, giving finance teams real-time control and visibility over company spending. Pemo serves more than 10,000 companies and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. Pemo does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company's identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Physiohome
companies.description: Physiohome, operating as Ameen (رعاية أمين), is a Saudi Arabia-based, tech-enabled provider of home rehabilitation and physical therapy services. Founded in 2021 out of a Ministry of Health sector accelerator, the company delivers physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, nutritional therapy, and personal training for adults and seniors in patients' homes and rehabilitation centers. Its platform manages the full care journey from assessment and treatment planning through session tracking, provider equipping, and reporting, with 100+ active service providers operating across nine cities and a wider network of 700+ providers. Ameen offers iOS and Android apps, an online booking flow, and a patient portal, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. It is a portfolio company of Sanabil 500 (500 Global) and Saudi Venture Capital.

companies.name: Thamarah Al-Jill Co LLC
companies.description: Thamarah Al-Jill Co LLC operates AMUSED Co (amusedco.com), a Saudi Arabia-based online marketplace for authenticated, curated pre-loved luxury — designer handbags and women's clothing from houses such as Louis Vuitton, Hermes and Chanel at up to 70% off retail. Under a "Resell, Rebuy, Relove" model, buyers shop verified second-hand pieces (backed by a one-year authentication money-back guarantee) and sellers list their own unused items; payment options include credit card, Mada and Tamara. The store is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is built on Shopify and is fully agent-native: it publishes an /llms.txt agent guide and implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) over an MCP endpoint, with Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect for buyer authentication.

companies.name: Ejari Co.
companies.description: Ejari (ايجاري) is a Riyadh-based property-technology and fintech company transforming the rental market in Saudi Arabia with a rent-now, pay-later (RNPL) model. Ejari pays a tenant's full annual rent to the landlord up front, then lets the tenant repay in twelve calm monthly installments, replacing the Kingdom's traditional single-cheque annual rent requirement. Founded in 2022 by Yazeed Al-Shamsi, Fahad Albedah, Mohammed Alkhelewy and Khalid Almunif, the company operates across 17+ Saudi cities and is building toward a full-service, Sharia-compliant real-estate super app. Ejari is backed by 500 Global and won the 2024 KPMG Global Tech Innovator competition.

companies.name: Stllr Network
companies.description: Stllr Network is an AI-powered user-generated-content (UGC) and creator-marketing platform for the Arab world, connecting brands with a network of nano and micro content creators and influencers across categories such as beauty, entertainment, tech, lifestyle, parenting, gaming, fashion, fitness, and cooking. Its products include Remix, an AI tool that scales creator videos into multiple ad variations; Premier, a managed service that handles creator outreach and ad-campaign management; and pay-as-you-go video Packages (PAYG). The platform is brand- and consumer-facing, billed in Saudi Riyal (SAR), and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Speero
companies.description: Speero (سبيرو) is Saudi Arabia's online marketplace for authentic automotive spare parts, accessories, and professional vehicle services. The platform helps car owners find OEM and aftermarket parts for their specific make and model across all major categories (engine, brakes, suspension, lighting, AC, exhaust, and more) and book maintenance, detailing, paint and dent repair, tinting, and tire care at trusted workshops across the Kingdom. It supports browse-by-vehicle, installment payment options, and WhatsApp-based customer support. Speero is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer marketplace and publishes no public developer API, but it does expose a machine-discovery surface (llms.txt, RFC 9116 security.txt, and an RFC 9727 api-catalog linkset).

companies.name: Nqoodlet
companies.description: Nqoodlet is a Saudi Arabia-based (Riyadh) corporate spend and expense management platform for businesses from SMEs to enterprises. It lets teams issue unlimited virtual and physical company cards, track every transaction in real time, manage and control cards from a single dashboard, and pay globally in local currency without conversion fees. Over 600 companies use Nqoodlet to streamline expense management, eliminate paperwork, and gain clearer visibility into company spending. It is backed by 500 Global. Nqoodlet does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures the company's public web identity plus a live domain-security probe.

companies.name: Drahim Holdings
companies.description: Drahim (دراهم) is a Saudi personal-finance and automated-investment fintech, founded in Riyadh in 2021 by Sultan Alkhayal and Yasser Alshurihi. Its mobile app uses open banking to aggregate a user's bank accounts into one view, enriches and auto-categorizes transactions (2.5B+ processed), and offers auto-savings, Zakat calculation, and Sharia-compliant robo-advisory portfolios spanning 40+ funds across Saudi and global equities, real estate, and commodities. Drahim is licensed by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) for open-banking/payment services and by the Capital Market Authority (CMA) for investment management; it was backed by Y Combinator and 500 Global, and Al Rajhi Bank acquired a 65% majority stake in 2024. Drahim is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate and product identity plus live domain-security posture. Consumer surfaces include the iOS and Android apps and a business platform.

companies.name: FIFOplus
companies.description: FIFOplus is a B2B smart-procurement marketplace for the HORECA sector (hotels, restaurants, cafes, and catering) in Saudi Arabia, connecting food-service buyers with suppliers across a webstore and mobile app that lists more than 5,000 food and non-food items spanning meat, seafood, dairy, produce, frozen goods, condiments, beverages, packaging, and cleaning supplies. The platform layers ordering, real-time order tracking, inventory, menu, and finance optimization with AI and integrates with point-of-sale systems and credit-terms payment. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Jeddah, FIFOplus operates across Jeddah, Makkah, Riyadh, and Taif and is backed by the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator (500 Global) and Palm Ventures. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; FIFOplus publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Gathern
companies.description: Gathern (جاذر) is the first licensed peer-to-peer vacation-rental marketplace in Saudi Arabia, founded in Riyadh in 2016 and licensed by the Saudi Ministry of Tourism. Through its iOS, Android, and web apps, travelers book short-term private accommodations directly from local hosts — chalets, apartments, villas, farms, resorts, rest houses (istrahat), camps, caravans, and rooms — across more than 200 cities and provinces in the Kingdom, including Riyadh, Jeddah, Taif, Al Khobar, Dammam, Mecca, Medina, and AlUla. The platform lists tens of thousands of units, has served more than five million users, and holds a leading share of the alternative-hospitality sector in Saudi Arabia. Backed by 500 Global, STV, Sanabil Investments (a Public Investment Fund subsidiary), and others, Gathern raised a $72M Series B and is preparing for a Tadawul listing. Gathern operates as a consumer marketplace app and does not currently publish a public developer API surface; this profile tracks its public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Safqah Holdings Limited
companies.description: Safqah Holdings Limited operates Safqah (Safqah Capital / Safqah Financial), a Saudi Arabian fintech platform headquartered in the Al-Malqa district of Riyadh and regulated by the Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA). Safqah provides Sharia-compliant, debt-based real estate investment opportunities that let qualified individual and institutional investors fund real estate development deals starting from 1,000 SAR, alongside a financing arm that offers land acquisition, residential development, commercial development, raw land, and bridge financing to real estate developers. Investors track deal performance through periodic reporting and live project camera feeds. The platform is a consumer- and investor-facing web application with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or integration surface at this time.

companies.name: Emtethal
companies.description: Emtethal is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia based smart compliance and inspection management platform for the food service and hospitality sectors, backed by 500 Global. The platform automates inspection scheduling and distribution, provides custom checklists per facility type, captures photo documentation with automatic timestamps and GPS location, detects and categorizes violations automatically, and pushes real-time alerts for critical issues. It layers analytics and compliance reporting on top of an offline-capable mobile field-inspection app (iOS and Android) and AI-powered camera and sensor monitoring. Emtethal serves both individual food facilities and consulting firms managing multiple client sites, offering a 14-day free trial. There is no public API, developer portal, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile is an API Evangelist company lead maintained for enrichment and monitoring.

companies.name: Happy World
companies.description: Happy World operates SPICE (getspice.com), a premium lifestyle dining and rewards mobile application based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. SPICE lets diners discover curated partner restaurants across the Kingdom, reserve or walk in, pay their bill in-app by entering the bill number, and earn instant cashback rewards (advertised as up to 20% cashback with no caps) on every visit. The product emphasizes intelligent personalization and a hand-picked selection of the best restaurants, food, and dining experiences. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The company is a consumer mobile-app business with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

companies.name: Awfar Market
companies.description: Awfar is a Cairo- and Riyadh-based digital solutions company (founded 2013) offering an integrated customer engagement and commerce platform. It combines an omnichannel Chat Center with AI agents (WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook), a cloud Call Center, and a Commerce & Delivery platform for order, inventory, and logistics management within a single interface. Awfar serves more than 2,000 clients across retail, pharmacy, restaurant, e-commerce, tourism, healthcare, education, and real estate, and ships prebuilt integrations for Shopify, Meta, Odoo, Zid, and Salla plus custom API connections. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal or OpenAPI specification is published at this time; integration is arranged via the sales and demo channel.

Juleb connects to Saudi compliance systems (ZATCA/Fatoora, RSD, GS1, Wasfaty), e-commerce channels (Salla, Shopify, HungerStation), payment providers (Geidea, Alhamrani), and ERPs (Microsoft Dynamics). Founded by Yousuf Jamjoom and backed by 500 Global, Juleb exposes a REST API (documented at docs.juleb.com) covering inventory, point of sale, prescriptions, and partner/company resources.

companies.name: CarSwitch
companies.description: CarSwitch is a tech-enabled used-car marketplace founded in Dubai in 2016 that facilitates buying and selling of pre-owned vehicles across the United Arab Emirates (Dubai, Abu Dhabi and nationwide) and Saudi Arabia. Rather than a traditional classifieds site, CarSwitch operates as a fully managed service: every car undergoes a 200-point inspection before listing, sellers get an end-to-end managed selling service (professional photography, listing, negotiation and RTA transfer handling), and buyers get price transparency, a free online car-valuation tool and installment financing through banking partners such as Emirates NBD, FAB, ADCB, ADIB, DIB and Emirates Islamic. The company has inspected 130,000+ vehicles and facilitated over $500 million in sales. CarSwitch was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a consumer marketplace with no public developer API program.

companies.name: Behja
companies.description: Behja (Behja Holdings Limited Inc) is a licensed real estate platform in Saudi Arabia (License 120022677) that offers flexible rental-to-own housing. Its model lets residents select a property, apply, sign a three-year lease, and then buy with a full year's rent credited back toward the purchase. The integrated platform handles leases, purchases, and utility payments in one place. Behja is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer program, API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

companies.name: ElMetr
companies.description: ElMetr (المتر) is a Middle East legal-tech company providing online legal consultation and guidance for companies, entrepreneurs, and individuals. The platform combines licensed lawyers with modern technology to connect users with qualified legal help, offering subscription legal packages that cover company formation and registration, contract review, compliance, intellectual property, and dispute resolution. Founded in Egypt and now operating in Saudi Arabia, ElMetr aims to make legal work clear, fast, and fair so businesses can move faster and reduce risk from first idea through expansion. ElMetr is a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. This company profile has been through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; ElMetr does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: MisMar
companies.description: MisMar (مسمار) is a Saudi Arabian automotive maintenance and repair platform that connects vehicle owners with certified service centers. It runs a consumer mobile app (B2C) alongside a Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) platform and Workshop Management System (WMS) that digitize fleet management, order processing, and workshop operations for business (B2B), government (B2G), and insurance partners. Services span fault diagnostics, accident restoration, oil and battery and tire changes, periodic maintenance, car wash, and protective treatments across 45+ Saudi cities, with at-home or center-based delivery and warranty coverage. MisMar is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is currently published.

companies.name: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD
companies.description: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD operates Moedatech (معداتك), Saudi Arabia's first digital procurement and rental marketplace for heavy construction equipment, connecting contractors with verified suppliers of excavators, cranes, and trucks through RFQs, real-time bidding, and audit-ready digital contracts. Founded in Riyadh in 2020 by Ali Merie and Mansour Hmaid, the company pairs the marketplace with a telematics/fleet layer (built on Traccar GPS tracking) so equipment owners can monitor real-time asset performance. The product ships as iOS and Android apps plus a web app; there is no publicly documented developer API at this time. The company is backed by 500 Global and Plug and Play Middle East. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from the company's public web, brand (moedatech.net), and GitHub presence.

companies.name: Desaisiv Inc.
companies.description: DESAISIV is a corporate InsurTech platform focused on health insurance in Saudi Arabia and the wider MENA region. Founded in 2022, the company builds AI and automation products for insurers and third-party administrators (TPAs), including smart underwriting automation, a real-time quotation engine, OCR-powered claims intelligence, a corporates insurance marketplace, and SME portals. Its platform bridges data, systems, insurers, and corporates to streamline underwriting, quoting, and claims. DESAISIV is backed by 500 Global, Terra VC, Oqal, and other MENA/UK/US investors via a US$2M pre-seed round. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

companies.name: Governata
companies.description: Governata is a Saudi Arabia-based data governance and management platform that helps government entities and enterprises turn complex data into business value through comprehensive, PDPL-aligned data management. Its product suite spans Data Governance (business glossary, data catalog, data classification, data lineage, metadata store, data quality), Master Data Management (domains, golden record, matching and survivorship), Data Privacy (personal-data discovery and protection under Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law, access management, and a service catalog), and Governata Core, an administrative backbone covering license management, audit trail, and workflows. Governata packages role-based solutions for chief data officers, compliance officers, data protection officers, and data stewards, and sector solutions for government, healthcare, financial services, insurance, telecom, retail, energy, and large enterprises. It is backed by 500 Global and is being profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification was found at the time of enrichment; this profile captures the company's identity and web presence.

companies.name: Trella
companies.description: Trella is a Cairo-headquartered B2B trucking marketplace and digital freight platform that connects shippers with carriers across the Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan (MENA-P). Founded in 2019 by Omar Hagrass, Ali El Atrash, and Pierre Saad and backed by Y Combinator, Trella runs a digital load marketplace, a carrier mobile app, and a shipper web dashboard that together replace the traditional broker-driven, paper-based long-haul trucking workflow. Core platform services include load posting and carrier matching, instant quoting, GPS tracking and live shipment visibility, electronic proof of delivery (ePODs), load insurance, a control-tower operations layer for carrier quality and performance, and integrated payments and invoicing between shippers and carriers. The network spans 30,000+ carriers and operates from major freight hubs including Cairo, Alexandria, Port Said, Damietta, Sokhna, Jeddah, Dammam, Riyadh, and Dubai, serving industries such as FMCG, construction, manufacturing, agriculture, mining, e-commerce, retail, electronics, ceramics, and freight forwarding. Trella's revenue model is marketplace take-rate and value-added logistics services; there is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks catalog, or open-source platform release for the Trella marketplace.

companies.name: Noon
companies.description: Noon is a Dubai-headquartered e-commerce marketplace and digital ecosystem launched in 2017 as a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Emirati businessman Mohamed Alabbar. Frequently described as the Amazon of the MENA region, Noon operates as the leading online shopping destination across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Egypt, offering electronics, mobiles, fashion, beauty, home, appliances, baby, and grocery categories through a hybrid first-party and third-party seller marketplace. Beyond the core marketplace, Noon has expanded into a lifestyle super-app spanning Noon Food (quick-service restaurant delivery competing with Talabat and Deliveroo), Noon Daily (next-day grocery delivery), Noon Minutes (15-minute instant grocery and essentials delivery), Noon Pay and the Noon mobile wallet (QR payments, bill pay, and a co-branded credit card), Noon VIP (loyalty/subscription), NowNow (on-demand delivery in KSA), and SIVVI (acquired regional fashion brand). Noon operates its own last-mile logistics arm and warehouses across the region, and provides a Fulfilled by Partner Integration (FBPI) program with commercial APIs that allow third-party sellers and channel-integration partners (ChannelEngine, Unicommerce, Vinculum, Ecom Energize and others) to programmatically publish catalog, sync inventory, and manage shipments. These APIs are gated to onboarded sellers and certified integrators inside the noon.partners environment — there is no general public developer portal, no published OpenAPI specification, and no Noon-maintained SDKs, CLIs, or open-source repositories.

companies.name: Sanad Cash
companies.description: Sanad Cash was a Saudi Arabia-based fintech startup that operated an on-demand payment platform, giving employees early access to earned wages and providing employers with tools to manage on-demand pay. The company raised a $1.6M seed round in January 2022 with participation from Impact46 and was backed by 500 Global. Sanad Cash was acquired by HyperPay in July 2023, and the Sanad Cash business was subsequently acquired by Qashio in October 2025. The independent sanadcash.com property is no longer reachable (no live HTTPS service), so this profile documents the company's identity and residual domain footprint rather than a live developer/API surface.

companies.name: Haseel
companies.description: Haseel (حصيل) is a Riyadh-based technology startup, founded in 2018, that delivers fresh fruits and vegetables to consumers across Saudi Arabia through its iOS and Android mobile apps. The company sources high-quality produce and fulfills each order from the nearest of its branches inside Riyadh, pairing a curated selection with fast, reliable last-mile delivery. Haseel reports more than 400,000 app downloads, three branches inside Riyadh, and over 1,000 orders per day, and is backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Haseel is a consumer produce-delivery app and does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Doos
companies.description: Doos is a Saudi-based quick-commerce (q-commerce) platform and mobile app that delivers groceries, fresh produce, beauty, gifting, pharmacy, and lifestyle products in minutes across Saudi Arabia. Founded in 2023 by Tala Al Sahsah, it operates cloud/dark stores in Jeddah and Riyadh with localised assortments, prices, and promotions by city and delivery zone, offering a bilingual (Arabic/English) shopping experience. Doos is backed by 500 Global and received a strategic investment from Jahez to accelerate its expansion in the Kingdom's growing quick-commerce sector. This is a consumer-facing storefront; no public developer program or API has been identified at this time.
